# Props

<!-- GENERATED by `scripts/gen-consumer-skills.mjs` — do not edit. Regenerate: `npm run consumer:gen` -->

Only props the kit declares itself. A component that also forwards its
underlying element's props — and they all do — accepts every attribute that
element accepts; those are not repeated here.

`className` is universal and never listed: every component merges it **last**,
so an app utility wins without `!important`. The two exceptions where it lands
on a wrapper instead are called out in the usage skill.

Components with no rows below declare no props of their own — they are the underlying primitive's API in full: `card`, `skeleton`.

## `<pkg>/alert`

### Alert

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colorPalette` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'black' \| 'red' \| 'green' \| 'yellow' \| 'third' \| null` | `'primary'` | — | The status, expressed as a hue: `red` for errors, `green` for success, `yellow` for warnings, `secondary` for information and `primary` for CBAR's emphasised `info-secondary`. Ignored by the shorthand variants. Defaults to `primary`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| null` | `'md'` | — | Padding, type size and glyph size together — 12 / 16 / 18px padding with a 16 / 20 / 24px icon. `sm` is what Figma calls `default`; the kit's default is `md`. |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'subtle' \| 'surface' \| 'outline' \| 'default' \| 'destructive' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| null` | `'solid'` | — | How filled in the alert is. `solid` is a full fill, `subtle` a tint, `surface` the tint plus a border, `outline` the border alone. The one-word `default` / `destructive` / `success` / `warning` shorthands pin their own colour and ignore `colorPalette`. Defaults to `solid`. |

## `<pkg>/badge`

### Badge

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | — | Render the child element instead of a `<span>` — e.g. to make it a link. |
| `colorPalette` | `VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants>['colorPalette']` | `'primary'` | — | Which CBAR ramp the treatment draws from — the hue that says *what kind* of thing the badge marks, while `variant` decides how loudly it says it. Note that `secondary` here is the turquoise ramp, not the grey `variant="secondary"` shorthand; the two names collide. Ignored by the shorthand variants, which pin their own colour. Defaults to `primary`. |
| `size` | `VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants>['size']` | `'md'` | — | Height, padding, type size and glyph size together — 16 / 20 / 24 / 28px tall. Match it to what the badge annotates rather than picking one house size: `xs` and `sm` ride inside a dense table cell or beside body copy without changing the line's rhythm, `lg` is for a badge standing alone in a header where `md` reads undersized. Defaults to `md`. |
| `variant` | `VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants>['variant']` | `'solid'` | — | How filled in the badge is. `solid` is a full fill and the loudest of the set — use it when the badge is the thing being read, not an annotation on something else; `subtle` and `surface` are the tint and the tint plus an outline, quiet enough to sit inside a table row; `outline` and `ghost` carry the least weight, for a marker that must not compete with the label beside it. The one-word `default` / `secondary` / `destructive` / `success` / `warning` shorthands pin their own colour and ignore `colorPalette`. Defaults to `solid`. |

### Combobox

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ComboboxOption[]` | — | yes | The rows to choose from, in the order they are listed. |

| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | — | Greys the trigger and stops it opening. The chosen value stays visible. |
| `emptyMessage` | `string` | `'No results found.'` | — | Shown in place of the list when no option matches the query. Defaults to `No results found.`. |
| `id` | `string` | — | — | Put it on the trigger, so a `<Label htmlFor>` can point at it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | — | Fires when the list opens or closes — from the trigger, a choice, Escape or an outside click. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | — | Called with the chosen option's `value`, or `''` when the selected option is chosen again and the selection clears. |
| `open` | `boolean` | — | — | Controlled open state of the list. Pair with `onOpenChange`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Select an option…'` | — | Shown on the trigger when nothing is selected. Also the trigger's accessible name when neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby` is given. Defaults to `Select an option…`. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `'Search…'` | — | Placeholder of the search box inside the list. Defaults to `Search…`. |
| `value` | `string` | — | — | Controlled selection. Pass with `onValueChange`. |

### DataTable

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `DataTableColumn<RecordType>[]` | — | yes | Column definitions, in display order. |

| `id` | `string` | — | — | `id` of the scroll container. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | — | — | Fills the body with placeholder rows while the data is on its way. Wins over `emptyText`. |
| `onRow` | `(record: RecordType, index?: number) => React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` | — | — | Extra attributes and handlers for each body `<tr>` — `onClick`, `className`, … |
| `onSortChange` | `(sort: DataTableSort \| null) => void` | — | — | Fires when a sortable header is clicked, cycling ascending → descending → `null`. Called in both modes; only in controlled mode is it also the one doing the sorting. |
| `rowClassName` | `string \| ((record: RecordType, index: number) => string)` | — | — | Class for every body row, or a function deciding it per record. |
| `rowKey` | `string \| ((record: RecordType, index?: number) => React.Key)` | `'key'` | — | Field name or function producing a stable key per row. Defaults to `key`. |
| `rowSelection` | `DataTableRowSelection<RecordType>` | — | — | Row selection. Passing the object adds a leading checkbox column with a select-all in its header. See DataTableRowSelection. |

| `sort` | `DataTableSort \| null` | — | — | Controlled sort. Pass it together with `onSortChange` when something else sorts the data (a server, a query hook). Leave both off and the table sorts its own rows. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | — | — | Keep the header visible while the table's container scrolls. |

| `max` | `number` | `Infinity` | — | Upper bound, applied on commit and exposed as `aria-valuemax`. Unbounded by default. |

| `parser` | `(displayValue: string) => number` | — | — | Turns a typed string back into a number. Required whenever `formatter` is set. |
| `precision` | `number` | — | — | Decimal places to round to on commit. Defaults to whatever `step` implies. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | — | How far one stepper click or arrow key moves the value. Its decimals also set the rounding when `precision` is not given, so `step={0.1}` keeps the value at one place. Defaults to `1`. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | — | — | Controlled value. `null` is an empty field; pair with `onChange`. |

Reach past the default when the ring reports an outcome rather than plain progress — `green` for a job that finished clean, `red` for one heading for a failure, `yellow` for a quota running out. Defaults to `primary`. |

Defaults to on from `md` up and off below it: `xs` and `sm` leave 16px and 22px of clear space inside the ring, and "100%" at CBAR's 12px needs about 30px, so the label spills over its own stroke. Pass `true` to force it — with a `formatValue` that returns something short enough to fit. |
| `size` | `VariantProps<typeof progressCircleVariants>['size']` | `'md'` | — | Ring diameter and stroke weight together — 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64px boxes carrying a 4 → 8px stroke. It also decides whether the percentage prints by default (see `showValue`), so the choice is as much about how much the ring has to say as how much room it has: `xs` and `sm` are a bare indicator for a table cell or a row of text, `md` and `lg` are the sizes that can still be read as a number, and `xl` is for a ring that is the subject of its own tile. Defaults to `md`. |

## `<pkg>/tree`

### Tree

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `treeData` | `TreeNode[]` | — | yes | The nodes to render, as a nested array of `TreeNode`. Every `key` must be unique across the whole tree, not just among siblings — it is what the `*Keys` props and callbacks refer to. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | — | Name announced for the whole tree. Give one whenever there is no visible heading to point `aria-labelledby` at. |
| `checkable` | `boolean` | — | — | Show checkboxes, with checked state propagating up and down. |
| `checkedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Controlled checked state, as **leaf** keys only. A branch is derived as checked when all of its leaves are and as indeterminate when some are. Pair with `onCheck`. |
| `defaultCheckedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Leaves checked on first render when `checkedKeys` is not controlled. |
| `defaultExpandAll` | `boolean` | — | — | Open every branch on first render. Convenient for small trees; a large tree is better served by `defaultExpandedKeys` or `virtual`. |
| `defaultExpandedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Branches open on first render when `expandedKeys` is not controlled. |
| `defaultSelectedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Node selected on first render when `selectedKeys` is not controlled. |
| `emptyText` | `React.ReactNode` | `'No data.'` | — | Shown in place of the rows when `treeData` is empty. Defaults to `No data.`. |
| `expandedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Controlled set of open branches. Pair with `onExpand`; leave unset to let the tree manage expansion itself. |
| `height` | `number` | — | — | Height of the scroll viewport in pixels. Required for `virtual` to take effect; ignored otherwise. |
| `itemHeight` | `number` | `28` | — | Row height, only used when `virtual` is set. Defaults to `28`. |
| `onCheck` | `(keys: React.Key[], info: TreeCheckInfo) => void` | — | — | Fires when a checkbox is toggled, with the checked leaf keys plus the node that changed and the branches now half-checked. Only meaningful with `checkable`. |
| `onExpand` | `(keys: React.Key[], info: { node: TreeNode; expanded: boolean }) => void` | — | — | Fires when a branch opens or closes, with the full set of open keys and the branch that changed. |
| `onSelect` | `(keys: React.Key[], info: { node: TreeNode; selected: boolean }) => void` | — | — | Fires on click, Enter, or Space (when not `checkable`). Clicking the selected node again deselects it, reported as an empty array and `selected: false`. |
| `selectedKeys` | `readonly React.Key[]` | — | — | Controlled selection. Selection is single: the array holds at most one key. Pair with `onSelect`. |
| `switcherIcon` | `(node: { isLeaf: boolean; expanded: boolean }) => React.ReactNode` | — | — | Override the expand/collapse affordance. |
| `virtual` | `boolean` | — | — | Window the rows. Needs `height`; worth it past a few hundred nodes. |

| `beforeUpload` | `(file: UploadFile, fileList: UploadFile[]) => BeforeUploadResult \| Promise<BeforeUploadResult>` | — | — | The gate before any bytes move. Return `false` to skip the file, a `File`/`Blob` to replace what is sent, or nothing to let it through. It is awaited, so an async check works. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` | — | — | Replaces the default surface entirely. Keep it non-interactive — it sits inside a `<label>`, where a nested button would fight it for the click. |
| `className` | `string` | — | — | Classes for the visible surface, the wrapping `<label>`. |
| `classNames` | `{ input?: string }` | — | — | Classes for the inner parts. `input` reaches the hidden file input. |
| `customRequest` | `(option: UploadRequestOption, info: { defaultRequest: (option: UploadRequestOption) => UploadRequestHandle }) => UploadRequestHandle \| void` | — | — | Take over the transfer entirely — resumable uploads, SDK clients, S3. |
| `data` | `Record<string, unknown> \| ((file: UploadFile) => Record<string, unknown> \| PromiseLike<Record<string, unknown>>)` | — | — | Extra form fields. A function is resolved per file. |
| `directory` | `boolean` | — | — | Pick a whole folder rather than individual files. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | — | — | Turn the input off and drop the surface to 50%; neither a click nor a drop reaches it. |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string>` | — | — | Extra request headers, e.g. an authorization token. |
| `id` | `string` | — | — | `id` for the hidden input, so an external `<label htmlFor>` can point at it. |
| `method` | `UploadRequestMethod` | `'POST'` | — | HTTP verb for the built-in transfer. Defaults to `POST`. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | — | — | Take every picked file rather than the first one. |
| `name` | `string` | `'file'` | — | Form field name the file is sent under. Defaults to `file`. |
| `onError` | `(error: UploadRequestError \| ProgressEvent, body: unknown, file: UploadFile) => void` | — | — | The transfer failed — a non-2xx status or a network error. |
| `onProgress` | `(event: UploadProgressEvent, file: UploadFile) => void` | — | — | A progress tick for one file — `event.percent` is 0–100 when known. |
| `onStart` | `(file: UploadFile) => void` | — | — | A transfer has begun. Fires after `beforeUpload` lets the file through. |
| `onSuccess` | `(response: unknown, file: UploadFile, xhr?: XMLHttpRequest) => void` | — | — | The transfer answered 2xx. `response` is the parsed body, or the raw text when it is not JSON. |
| `openFileDialogOnClick` | `boolean` | `true` | — | Set `false` to open the picker yourself, e.g. from a button elsewhere. |
| `variant` | `VariantProps<typeof uploadVariants>['variant']` | `'dropzone'` | — | The surface: `dropzone` (the default) is the dashed drop target; `button` is a plain outline trigger for toolbars and form rows. Only the dropzone advertises itself as a drop target. |
| `withCredentials` | `boolean` | — | — | Send cookies on a cross-origin request. |

### UploadDropzone

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hint` | `React.ReactNode` | `'Up to 10 MB each'` | — | The quieter line under it — a size or file-type policy. Defaults to "Up to 10 MB each"; pass `null` to drop it. |
| `title` | `React.ReactNode` | `'Drop files here, or click to browse'` | — | The headline. Defaults to "Drop files here, or click to browse". |

## `<pkg>/virtual-list`

### VirtualList

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `(item: T, index: number) => React.ReactElement` | — | yes | Renders one row. The element must be exactly `itemHeight` tall — the list positions rows by arithmetic, not by measuring them. |
| `data` | `readonly T[]` | — | yes | Rows to render. Only the visible slice is mounted. |
| `height` | `number` | — | yes | Pixel height of the scroll viewport. |
| `itemHeight` | `number` | — | yes | Pixel height of one row. Rows must all be this tall. |
| `itemKey` | `keyof T \| ((item: T) => React.Key)` | — | yes | Stable key per row — an index is not enough once the list reorders. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | — | Accessible name of the scroll viewport, which is a `group`. It is in the tab order, so give it one when nothing nearby says what the list holds. |
| `className` | `string` | — | — | Classes for the scroll viewport; it already has a border and a fixed `height`. |
| `onScroll` | `React.UIEventHandler<HTMLElement>` | — | — | Fires when the viewport scrolls. Use it to trigger infinite loading. |
| `overscan` | `number` | `3` | — | Rows kept mounted above and below the viewport. A few rows of slack mean a fast scroll reveals content rather than blank space. Defaults to `3`. |
